note: Every URL this application is permitted to contact, as data rather than code. src/main/checker/fetch.js will request a URL only if it appears verbatim in this file; anything else is a hard error, not a request. Sizes and counts were measured on 2026-08-28 and will drift — they are recorded to show the order of magnitude, not as a contract.

sources.label: PhishDestroy
sources.maintainer: The PhishDestroy project, running since 2019. Curated active scam and phishing domains, published to GitHub and served through the jsDelivr CDN, which imposes no rate limits.

sources.label: Scam Blocklist
sources.maintainer: jarelllama on GitHub. Focuses on newly registered scam domains, retrieved from search engine results and threat feeds rather than from user reports alone.

sources.label: CyberHost Malware & Phishing Blocklist
sources.attribution: CyberHost Malware & Phishing Blocklist — https://cyberhost.uk/malware-blocklist/ — licensed CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.maintainer: CyberHost (cyberhost.uk). Aggregated from public threat intelligence, infosec communities and user submissions. Every entry is preceded by a comment naming the source it came from and the date it was added, which is why the file has roughly twice as many lines as domains.

excluded.reason: NonCommercial. DiskWatch is MIT, which permits commercial use downstream and cannot be revoked, so shipping code that fetches this feed would walk a commercial user into violating its terms. The OSI and the FSF both treat NC as non-free for this reason. It was the second-largest source considered (156,735 entries on 2026-08-28) and is deliberately absent rather than merely unlisted. Do not re-propose it without a licence change at the source.
